ex.en: Fifty pounds is the best I can offer you.
ex.cn: 我顶多出五十英镑。

ex.en: The best we can hope for in the game is a draw.
ex.cn: 我们至多能希望比赛打成平局。

senses.def: the highest standard that a particular person has reached, especially in a sport

ex.en: a lifetime best of 12.0 seconds
ex.cn: 12.0 秒的毕生最好成绩

senses.def: used when you are saying goodbye to sb or ending a letter, to give sb your good wishes
senses.chn: （告别用语或书信结语）祝一切顺利，万事如意

senses.def: used for saying what is the best opinion you can have of sb/sth, or the best thing that can happen, when the situation is bad
senses.chn: （表达最正面的看法或恶劣状况下可能出现的最好转机）充其量

ex.en: Their response to the proposal was, at best, cool.
ex.cn: 他们对提议的反应充其量只能说是漠然置之。

ex.en: We can't arrive before Friday at best.
ex.cn: 我们无论如何星期五之前也到不了。

senses.def: used to say that although sth appears bad or unpleasant now, it will be good in the end

ex.en: I don't want you to leave, but perhaps it's for the best.
ex.cn: 我并不想让你走，但也许还是走的好。

senses.def: a person or thing that is a little better than the rest of a group, although none are very good
senses.chn: 一群（或堆）坏的里较好者；矮子中的将军

senses.def: up to three, five, etc. games played to decide who wins, the winner being the person who wins most of them
senses.chn: 三局两胜（或五局三胜等）

senses.def: the very best

ex.en: We make sure our clients get the best that money can buy.
ex.cn: 我们确保客户买到最好的产品。

senses.def: to do or say sth in order to achieve a good result or to help sb
senses.chn: 为美好的目的；出于好意

ex.en: I just don't know what to do for the best.
ex.cn: 我就是弄不清做什么才好。

ex.en: I'm sorry if my advice offended you—I meant it for the best.
ex.cn: 如果我的建议冒犯了你，我很抱歉。但我原本是出于好意。

senses.def: to gain more advantage from sth than sb else

ex.en: I thought you had the best of that discussion.
ex.cn: 我以为你在那场讨论中占了上风。

senses.def: to accept a bad or difficult situation and do as well as you can
as far as you know

ex.en: He never made a will, to the best of my knowledge.
ex.cn: 据我所知，他从未立过遗嘱。

senses.def: as well as anyone
senses.chn: 不亚于任何人；不比任何人差

ex.en: He'll be out there, dancing with the best of them.
ex.cn: 他将出现在舞池中，跳得不亚于任何人。

senses.def: the best out of a group of people or things
senses.chn: 出类拔萃的人（或事物）；精英；精品

senses.def: to hope that sth will happen successfully, especially where it seems likely that it will not
senses.chn: 希望某事顺利；寄予最大的希望

senses.def: used to wish sb success with sth

ex.en: The best of luck with your exams.
ex.cn: 祝你考试成功！

ex.en: Good luck! I hope it goes well.
ex.cn: 祝你交好运！我希望这事进展顺利。

senses.def: your best clothes
to defeat or be more successful than sb

be staring sb in the face.lemma: be staring sb in the face

senses.def: to be obvious or easy to see

ex.en: The answer was staring us in the face.
ex.cn: 答案明摆在我们面前。

senses.def: to be certain to happen

ex.en: Defeat was staring them in the face.
ex.cn: 他们必遭失败。

be staring sth in the face.lemma: be staring sth in the face

senses.def: to be unable to avoid sth

ex.en: They were staring defeat in the face.
ex.cn: 对他们来说，失败不可避免。

senses.def: a date printed on a container or package, advising you to use food or drink before this date as it will not be of such good quality after that
senses.chn: 最佳食用期限，最佳保质期，保存期限（见于食物或饮料包装）

senses.def: the assistant to the person in charge of the electrical equipment used when making a film/movie
senses.chn: （电影制作的）器材助理，灯光助理

senses.def: to have a lot of a particular quality

ex.en: a city steeped in history
ex.cn: 历史古城

senses.def: cruel and disgusting; of or like a beast
senses.chn: 凶残的；野兽的；野兽般的；兽性的

ex.en: bestial acts/cruelty/noises
ex.cn: 毫无人性的行为／残忍；野兽般的喧闹声

senses.def: sexual activity between a human and an animal
cruel or disgusting behaviour
a collection of descriptions of, or stories about, various types of animal, especially one written in the Middle Ages
a person's best friend

ex.en: It was fun hanging out with my bestie.
ex.cn: 那时候跟好友一起出去玩真开心。

ex.en: Hank is besties with Sarah.
ex.cn: 汉克跟萨拉是死党。

senses.def: to start doing things after a period during which you have been doing nothing
a male friend or relative of the bridegroom at a wedding, who helps him during the wedding ceremony
to give sth to sb, especially to show how much they are respected

ex.en: It was a title bestowed upon him by the king.
ex.cn: 那是国王赐给他的头衔。

senses.def: a way of doing sth that is seen as a very good example of how it should be done and can be copied by other companies or organizations
senses.chn: （公司或机构的）最佳实践，最佳做法

senses.def: to sit with one leg on either side of sth

ex.en: He bestrode his horse.
ex.cn: 他骑上马。

senses.def: to be good at sth

ex.en: I'm not very strong on dates (= I can't remember the dates of important events).
ex.cn: 我不大记得住日期。

senses.def: to have a lot of sth
senses.chn: 某事物有很多；强于某一方面

ex.en: The report was strong on criticism, but short on practical suggestions.
ex.cn: 这份报告批评的话说得多，但可行的建议提得少。

senses.def: a product, usually a book, which is bought by large numbers of people

ex.en: the bestseller list
ex.cn: 畅销书榜

senses.def: wearing a suit

ex.en: besuited businessmen
ex.cn: 身着套装的商界人员

senses.def: to be in a state of unhappiness or deep thought

ex.en: She just sat there, sunk in thought.
ex.cn: 她只一味地坐在那儿，陷入了沉思。

senses.def: used to tell sb to do sth

ex.en: Be sure to give your family my regards.
ex.cn: 务必代我向你的家人问好。

ex.en: Be sure and call me tomorrow.
ex.cn: 明天一定要打电话给我。

senses.def: to like sb very much in a romantic way
to risk money on a race or an event by trying to predict the result

ex.en: You have to be over 16 to bet.
ex.cn: 赌博者年龄不得低于 16 岁。

ex.en: I wouldn't bet on them winning the next election.
ex.cn: 下一次选举我不会赌他们赢。

ex.en: He bet $2 000 on the final score of the game.
ex.cn: 他下 2 000 美元赌比赛的最后比分。

ex.en: She bet me £20 that I wouldn't do it.
ex.cn: 她和我打 20 英镑的赌，说我不会那么做。

senses.def: used to say that you are almost certain that sth is true or that sth will happen

ex.en: I bet (that) we're too late.
ex.cn: 我们八成儿太晚了。

ex.en: You can bet (that) the moment I sit down, the phone will ring.
ex.cn: 几乎可以肯定，我一坐下，电话铃就会响起来。

ex.en: I'll bet you (that) he knows all about it.
ex.cn: 我敢说他了解一切。

senses.def: used to show that you can understand what sb is feeling, describing, etc.

ex.en: 'I nearly died when he told me.' 'I bet!'
ex.cn: “他告诉我时，我差一点死掉了。” “肯定是这样！”

senses.def: used to tell sb that you do not believe what they have just said

ex.en: 'I'm going to tell her what I think of her.' 'Yeah, I bet!'
ex.cn: “我要告诉她我对她的看法。” “谅你不敢！”

senses.def: used to say that you do not think that sth is very likely

ex.en: 'She'll soon get used to the idea.' 'I wouldn't bet on it.'
ex.cn: “她很快就会接受这种看法的。” “很难说。”

senses.def: used instead of 'yes' to emphasize that sb has guessed sth correctly or made a good suggestion

ex.en: 'Are you nervous?' 'You bet!'
ex.cn: “你紧张吗？” “这还用说！”

senses.def: used to say that you are certain that sth will happen

ex.en: You can bet your bottom dollar that he'll be late.
ex.cn: 他肯定会迟到。

senses.def: to risk everything you have on an investment, a bet, etc.

ex.en: The company bet the farm on the new marketing model, only to find that it wasn't successful.
ex.cn: 公司把全部身家都赌在了新的营销模式上，结果却并不成功。

senses.def: an arrangement to risk money, etc. on the result of a particular event; the money that you risk in this way

ex.en: to win/lose a bet
ex.cn: 赢／输一场赌

ex.en: We've got a bet on who's going to arrive first.
ex.cn: 我们打了个赌，看谁先到。

ex.en: He had a bet on the horses.
ex.cn: 他在那些马上下了赌注。

ex.en: They all put a bet on the race.
ex.cn: 他们都对比赛下了赌注。

ex.en: I hear you're taking bets on whether she'll marry him.
ex.cn: 我听说你在拿她是否会嫁给他的事和人打赌。

ex.en: I did it for a bet (= because sb had agreed to pay me money if I did).
ex.cn: 我是为了打赌才这么干的。

senses.def: an opinion about what is likely to happen or to have happened

ex.en: My bet is that they've been held up in traffic.
ex.cn: 我估计他们是堵车了。

senses.def: used to say that if a particular event happens then your current forecast, agreement, etc. will no longer apply

ex.en: We expect shares to rise unless the economy slows down again, in which case all bets are off.
ex.cn: 我们预计股票会涨，除非经济再次下滑。如果真是那样的话，结局就难料了。

senses.def: used to tell sb what is the best action for them to take to get the result they want

ex.en: If you want to get around London fast, the Underground is your best bet.
ex.cn: 如果你想在伦敦四处转转而又不费时间，最好是乘地铁。

senses.def: something that is likely to happen, to succeed or to be suitable
senses.chn: 很可能发生的事；有望成功的事；合适的东西

ex.en: Clothes are a safe bet as a present for a teenager.
ex.cn: 衣服适合作为送给十几岁孩子的礼物。

senses.def: to reduce the risk of losing or making a mistake by supporting more than one side in a competition, an argument, etc., or by having several choices available to you
senses.chn: （为防止损失或出错）几面下注，有几项选择可选取

senses.def: the second letter of the Greek alphabet (B, β)
senses.chn: 希腊字母表的第 2 个字母

senses.def: a drug used to control heart rhythm, treat severe chest pain and reduce high blood pressure
senses.chn: * β 阻滞药（用以控制心率、治疗严重胸部疼痛和降低血压）

senses.def: a substance found in carrots and other plants, which is needed by humans
the breaking up of an atom in which an electron is given off
senses.chn: * β 衰变（指原子分裂并释放出一个电子）

senses.def: to go somewhere

ex.en: He betook himself to his room.
ex.cn: 他进了自己的房间。

senses.def: a fast-moving electron that is produced when some radioactive substances decay
a test on a new product, done by sb who does not work for the company that is developing the product
senses.chn: * β 测试（外部对公司新产品的测试）

senses.def: a version of a product, especially computer software, that is almost ready for the public to buy or use, and that is tested by people who do not work for the company that is developing it
senses.chn: （尤指计算机软件等新产品上市前的）β 版，测试版

senses.def: the leaves of a climbing plant, also called betel, chewed by people in Asia
the slightly bitter nut of a tropical Asian palm, that is cut into small pieces, wrapped in betel leaves, and chewed
despite that

ex.en: I know that he has tried hard; be that as it may, his work is just not good enough.
ex.cn: 我知道他已经尽力了，尽管如此，他的工作仍不太理想。

senses.def: to be very good
to be very good; to be the best

ex.en: Check out the new website. It's the bomb!
ex.cn: 看一看这新网站。简直是太棒了！

senses.def: to be very good
to be the person or thing that other people often joke about or criticize
senses.chn: 受到嘲讽（或批评）；是笑柄（或话柄等）

ex.en: She was the butt of some very unkind jokes.
ex.cn: 她受到了刻薄的嘲弄。

senses.def: to worry or upset sb very much
senses.chn: 让某人担心得要命；使某人深感不安

ex.en: Those kids will be the death of me.
ex.cn: 为那些孩子操心会把我累死。

senses.def: to make sb worried or unhappy, because they cannot help

ex.en: My handwriting was the despair of my teachers.
ex.cn: 我的字写得很差，使老师们感到十分失望。

senses.def: to be socially acceptable behaviour
senses.chn: 是合乎礼仪的行为；是得体的行为

senses.def: when you say that people or situations are the end, you mean that you are annoyed with them
senses.chn: 令人讨厌；惹人烦恼；让人无法容忍

senses.def: to be very good or impressive
senses.chn: 非常好；给人以深刻印象

senses.def: to be extremely annoying
to make sb become a better or more successful person
senses.chn: 使成为更好（或更有作为）的人

ex.en: University was the making of Joe.
ex.cn: 大学造就了乔。

senses.def: to be very bad or the worst example of sth
senses.chn: 是坏典型；是拙劣典型；最糟糕

senses.def: to be available if sb wants to talk to you or if they need help

ex.en: You know I'll always be there for you.
ex.cn: 你知道我将永远在你左右。

be the spitting image of sb.lemma: be the spitting image of sb

senses.def: to look exactly like sb else

ex.en: She's the spitting image of her mother.
ex.cn: 她长得酷似她的母亲。

senses.def: to be intended for a particular purpose
be the end

ex.en: It's tickets for the team that loses.
ex.cn: 落败的球队就此止步。

senses.def: to be very pleased or amused
a phrase that is used to warn sb that there will be trouble for them if they do sth or do not do sth
senses.chn: （用以警告某人会有麻烦）…就要倒霉，…将会遭殃

ex.en: Woe betide anyone who gets in her way!
ex.cn: 谁挡住她的路谁就会遭殃！

senses.def: to be likely to die or be destroyed

ex.en: One mistake and you're toast.
ex.cn: 要是出一次错，你就完了。

senses.def: to be a sign of sth

ex.en: a clear blue sky betokening a fine day
ex.cn: 预示着好天气的晴朗蓝天

senses.def: happening after the time when it is possible to do sth

ex.en: It's too late to save her now.
ex.cn: 现在来拯救她的生命已为时太晚。

ex.en: Buy now before it's too late.
ex.cn: 欲购从速，勿失良机。

senses.def: to have a small amount of a particular quality

ex.en: His hair was touched with grey.
ex.cn: 他的头发有些斑白。

senses.def: to give information about sb/sth to an enemy

ex.en: He was offered money to betray his colleagues.
ex.cn: 有人收买他出卖他的同事。

ex.en: For years they had been betraying state secrets to Russia.
ex.cn: 他们多年来一直向俄罗斯泄露国家机密。

senses.def: to hurt sb who trusts you, especially by not being loyal or faithful to them

ex.en: She felt betrayed when she found out the truth about him.
ex.cn: 她发现他的真实情况时，感到受了欺骗。

ex.en: She betrayed his trust over and over again.
ex.cn: 她一次又一次地辜负了他的信任。

ex.en: I have never known her to betray a confidence (= tell other people sth that should be kept secret).
ex.cn: 我从未听说过她泄露秘密。

ex.en: She is accused of attempting to cheat the taxman.
ex.cn: 她被指控企图蒙骗税务员。

ex.en: He cheated his way into the job.
ex.cn: 他骗取了这份工作。

ex.en: You're not allowed to look at the answers— that's cheating.
ex.cn: 你们不许看答案，那是作弊。

senses.def: to ignore your principles or beliefs in order to achieve sth or gain an advantage for yourself

ex.en: He has been accused of betraying his former socialist ideals.
ex.cn: 有人指责他背弃了他先前的社会主义理想。

senses.def: to tell sb or make them aware of a piece of information, a feeling, etc., usually without meaning to

ex.en: His voice betrayed the worry he was trying to hide.
ex.cn: 他的声音掩盖不了内心的担忧。

ex.en: She was terrified of saying something that would make her betray herself (= show her feelings or who she was).
ex.cn: 她害怕说话时露了自己的底。

senses.def: the act of betraying sb/sth or the fact of being betrayed

ex.en: a sense/a feeling/an act of betrayal
ex.cn: 被出卖的感觉；背叛行为

ex.en: I saw her actions as a betrayal of my trust.
ex.cn: 我认为她的所作所为辜负了我的信任。

ex.en: the many disappointments and betrayals in his life
ex.cn: 他一生中遭受的诸多失望与背叛

senses.def: an agreement to marry sb
having promised to marry sb
the person that sb has promised to marry
senses.chn: 已订婚的人；未婚妻（或夫）

senses.def: of a higher standard or less poor quality; not as bad as sth else

ex.en: We're hoping for better weather tomorrow.
ex.cn: 我们希望明天天气转好。

ex.en: Her work is getting better and better.
ex.cn: 她的工作干得越来越好了。

ex.en: He is in a much better mood than usual.
ex.cn: 他的情绪比平时好多了。

ex.en: The meal couldn't have been better.
ex.cn: 这顿饭再好吃不过了。

ex.en: There's nothing better than a long soak in a hot bath.
ex.cn: 没有什么比好好地泡个热水澡更舒服的了。

ex.en: If you can only exercise once a week, that's better than nothing (= better than taking no exercise at all).
ex.cn: 即便是一个星期锻炼一次，也比完全不锻炼好。

senses.def: more able or skilled

ex.en: She's far better at science than her brother.
ex.cn: 她在理科方面比她的弟弟强得多。

senses.def: more suitable or appropriate

ex.en: Can you think of a better word than 'nice'?
ex.cn: 你能找到一个比 nice 更合适的字眼吗？

ex.en: It would be better for him to talk to his parents about his problems.
ex.cn: 他把自己的问题同父母谈谈会比较好。

ex.en: You'd be better going by bus.
ex.cn: 你坐公共汽车去会更好些。

senses.def: less ill/sick or unhappy
senses.chn: （病势）好转的，见轻的；舒畅些的

ex.en: She's a lot better today.
ex.cn: 她今天好多了。

ex.en: His leg was getting better.
ex.cn: 他的腿在渐渐恢复。

ex.en: You'll feel all the better for a good night's sleep.
ex.cn: 你晚上睡个好觉就会感觉好得多。

senses.def: fully recovered after an illness; in good health again

ex.en: Don't go back to work until you are better.
ex.cn: 身体康复之前，不要回去工作。

senses.def: almost or just the same as; almost or just as bad as
senses.chn: 同…（几乎）一样；和…（几乎）一样坏

ex.en: The path was no better than a sheep track.
ex.cn: 那条小路简直就像是给羊群踏出来的。

senses.def: used to give support to sb who has been upset and is trying to become calmer
senses.chn: （安慰他人时说）很好，这就对了

ex.en: Dry your eyes now. That's better.
ex.cn: 把眼泪擦干。这就对了。

senses.def: used to praise sb who has made an effort to improve
senses.chn: （称赞努力加以改进的人）很好

ex.en: That's much better—you played the right notes this time.
ex.cn: 很好，你这次把音弹准了。

senses.def: used to say that sth should be as big, small, etc. as possible

ex.en: I love giving parties, the bigger the better.
ex.cn: 我喜欢开派对，越盛大越好。

senses.def: you should avoid danger and not take unnecessary risks
senses.chn: 谨慎即大勇；慎重为勇敢之本

senses.def: used to say that two people can achieve more than one person working alone
most of sth, especially a period of time; more than half of sth

ex.en: The journey took her the better part of an hour.
ex.cn: 旅程花去了她半个多小时。

senses.def: it is better to stop sth bad from happening rather than try to deal with the problems after it has happened
senses.chn: 预防优于补救；防患于未然是上策

senses.def: in a more excellent or pleasant way; not as badly

ex.en: She sings much better than I do.
ex.cn: 她唱歌比我好得多。

ex.en: Sound travels better in water than in air.
ex.cn: 声音在水中比在空气中传播得快。

ex.en: People are better educated now.
ex.cn: 现在人们教育程度更高了。

senses.def: more; to a greater degree

ex.en: You'll like her when you know her better.
ex.cn: 你对她了解得多一点就会喜欢她。

ex.en: A cup of tea? There's nothing I'd like better!
ex.cn: 一杯茶吗？那最好不过了！

ex.en: Fit people are better able to cope with stress.
ex.cn: 健康的人较能应付压力。

senses.def: used to suggest that sth would be a suitable or appropriate thing to do

ex.en: The money could be better spent on more urgent cases.
ex.cn: 这笔钱用于较紧迫的事情也许会好些。

ex.en: Some things are better left unsaid.
ex.cn: 有些事还是不提为好。

ex.en: You'd do better to tell her everything before she finds out from someone else.
ex.cn: 你把一切都告诉她才是上策，免得她从别人口中听到。

senses.def: to have more money

ex.en: Families will be better off under the new law.
ex.cn: 新法律会使家庭经济宽裕一些。

ex.en: Her promotion means she's $100 a week better off.
ex.cn: 她的晋升意味着她每星期多挣 100 美元。

senses.def: used to say that sb is/would be happier or more satisfied if they were in a particular position or did a particular thing
senses.chn: （在某情况下或因做某事）更幸福，更满意

ex.en: She's better off without him.
ex.cn: 没有他，她活得更幸福。

ex.en: The weather was so bad we'd have been better off staying at home.
ex.cn: 天气非常恶劣，我们还不如待在家里舒服。

senses.def: used to tell sb what you think they should do
senses.chn: （告诉别人应该做的事）应该，最好

ex.en: You'd better go to the doctor about your cough.
ex.cn: 你最好去找医生看看你的咳嗽。

ex.en: We'd better leave now or we'll miss the bus.
ex.cn: 我们最好现在就走，不然就赶不上公共汽车了。

ex.en: You'd better not do that again.
ex.cn: 你最好别再这样做了。

ex.en: 'I'll give you back the money tomorrow.' 'You'd better!' (= as a threat)
ex.cn: “我明天会还你钱。” “那样最好！”

ex.en: If you think it is going to be easy, you'd best think again.
ex.cn: 如果你认为那会很容易，你最好再想想。

ex.en: You should take the baby to the doctor's.
ex.cn: 你应该把这婴儿带去看看医生。

senses.def: something that is better

ex.en: the better of the two books
ex.cn: 两本书中较好的一本

ex.en: I expected better of him (= I thought he would have behaved better).
ex.cn: 我本以为他会表现得好一些。

senses.def: people who are more intelligent or more important than you
senses.chn: 更有才智者；更重要的人

senses.def: used to say that sth cannot be changed, whether the result is good or bad
senses.chn: 不论好坏；不管是福是祸；不管怎样

senses.def: to defeat sb/sth or gain an advantage

ex.en: No one can get the better of her in an argument.
ex.cn: 辩论起来没人能辩过她。

ex.en: She always gets the better of an argument.
ex.cn: 她在争辩中总是占上风。

ex.en: His curiosity got the better of him (= he didn't intend to ask questions, but he wanted to know so badly that he did).
ex.cn: 好奇心使得他不禁要问。

senses.def: used to say that sth is even better/worse

ex.en: We don't actually need it on Tuesday, but if it arrives by then, so much the better.
ex.cn: 实际上我们星期二并不需要它，但如果那时能到就更好。

senses.def: a person, thing, situation, etc. that is better/worse than the previous or present one
people who are older and wiser than you and whom you should respect
to have a higher opinion of sb

ex.en: She has behaved appallingly—I must say I thought better of her.
ex.cn: 她的行为太恶劣了，看来我过去是高看了她。

senses.def: to be better or do sth better than sb/sth else

ex.en: The work he produced early in his career has never really been bettered.
ex.cn: 他后来没出过什么作品能真正比得上他的早期作品。

senses.def: to improve your social position through education, a better job, etc.
senses.chn: （通过教育、更好的工作等）改进社会地位，上进

ex.en: Thousands of Victorian workers joined educational associations in an attempt to better themselves.
ex.cn: 维多利亚时代成千上万名工人加入了各种教育协会，以求上进。

senses.def: used especially when you, or sb else, arrive/arrives late, or when sth such as success happens late, to say that this is better than not coming or happening at all
senses.chn: 迟到总比不到好；迟发生总比不发生强

senses.def: used to encourage sb who has not been successful at sth
senses.chn: （鼓励未成功的人）祝下次好运

senses.def: the process of becoming or making sth/sb better
used to say that it is wiser to be too careful than to act too quickly and do sth you may later wish you had not
senses.chn: 宁可事先谨慎有余，不要事后追悔莫及

senses.def: the act of risking money, etc. on the unknown result of an event

ex.en: illegal betting
ex.cn: 非法赌博

senses.def: it seems likely that…

ex.en: What's the betting that he gets his own way?
ex.cn: 你认为他可能会自行其是吗？

ex.en: The betting is that he'll get his own way.
ex.cn: 他很可能会自行其是。

senses.def: a shop where you can bet on horse races and other competitions
in or into the space separating two or more points, objects, people, etc.

ex.en: Q comes between P and R in the English alphabet.
ex.cn: 英语字母表中，Q 在 P 和 R 之间。

ex.en: I sat down between Jo and Diana.
ex.cn: 我在乔和黛安娜中间坐下。

ex.en: Switzerland lies between France, Germany, Austria and Italy.
ex.cn: 瑞士位于法国、德国、奥地利和意大利之间。

ex.en: The paper had fallen down between the desk and the wall.
ex.cn: 那张纸掉在桌子和墙壁之间的缝隙里。

ex.en: My job is somewhere between a secretary and a personal assistant.
ex.cn: 我的工作介于秘书和私人助理之间。

senses.def: in the period of time that separates two days, years, events, etc.

ex.en: It's cheaper between 6 p.m. and 8 a.m.
ex.cn: 下午 6 点到早晨 8 点间价钱较便宜。

ex.en: Don't eat between meals.
ex.cn: 正餐之间不要吃零食。

ex.en: Children must attend school between the ages of 5 and 16.
ex.cn: 5 到 16 岁的孩子必须上学。

ex.en: Many changes took place between the two world wars.
ex.cn: 两次世界大战之间发生了很多变化。

senses.def: at some point along a scale from one amount, weight, distance, etc. to another

ex.en: It weighed between nine and ten kilos.
ex.cn: 重量在九到十公斤之间。

ex.en: The temperature remained between 25°C and 30°C all week.
ex.cn: 整个星期气温都保持在 25 到 30 摄氏度之间。

senses.def: separating one place from another

ex.en: the border between Sweden and Norway
ex.cn: 瑞典和挪威之间的边界

senses.def: from one place to another
senses.chn: 从（一地）到（另一地）；往返于

ex.en: We fly between Rome and Paris twice daily.
ex.cn: 我们每天有两次航班往返于罗马和巴黎之间。

senses.def: used to show a connection or relationship

ex.en: a difference/distinction/contrast between two things
ex.cn: 两事物之间的差异／区别／对比

ex.en: a link between unemployment and crime
ex.cn: 失业与犯罪之间的关联

ex.en: There's a lot of bad feeling between them.
ex.cn: 他们彼此间芥蒂颇多。

ex.en: I had to choose between the two jobs.
ex.cn: 我得在两份工作之间作出选择。

senses.def: shared by two or more people or things

ex.en: We ate a pizza between us.
ex.cn: 我们合吃了一张比萨饼。

ex.en: This is just between you and me / between ourselves (= it is a secret).
ex.cn: 这事只限我们两人知道。

senses.def: by putting together the efforts or actions of two or more people or groups

ex.en: We ought to be able to manage it between us.
ex.cn: 我们齐心协力应该能把这事办妥。

senses.def: used to show that several activities are involved

ex.en: Between working full-time and taking care of the kids, he didn't have much time for hobbies.
ex.cn: 他一边全职工作一边又要照顾孩子，所以抽不出很多时间搞业余爱好。

senses.def: in the space or period of time separating two or more points, objects, etc. or two dates, events, etc.

ex.en: The house was near a park but there was a road in between.
ex.cn: 房子在一处公园附近，但两者之间隔着一条马路。

ex.en: I see her most weekends but not very often in between.
ex.cn: 我周末大多都能见到她，但平时不常见到。

between the devil and the deep blue sea.lemma: between the devil and the deep blue sea

senses.def: in a difficult situation where there are two equally unpleasant or unacceptable choices
between
in a middle position; neither one thing nor the other
in a middle position; neither one thing nor the other
to have weapons and be ready to fight in a war
senses.chn: 处于备战状态；严阵以待；枕戈待旦

senses.def: to be being dealt with successfully
senses.chn: 被控制住；处于控制之下

ex.en: Don't worry—everything's under control!
ex.cn: 别担心，一切都控制住了！

be up against a brick wall.lemma: be up against a brick wall

senses.def: to be unable to make any progress because there is a difficulty that stops you
to be in a very difficult situation
used in a formal situation to tell people to stand up

ex.en: Ladies and gentlemen, please be upstanding and join me in a toast to the bride and groom.
ex.cn: 各位来宾，请大家起立，我们一起为新娘新郎干一杯。

senses.def: to be sb's duty or responsibility; to be for sb to decide
senses.chn: 是…的职责（或责任）；由…决定

ex.en: It's not up to you to tell me how to do my job.
ex.cn: 还轮不到你来告诉我怎么做我的事。

ex.en: Shall we eat out or stay in? It's up to you.
ex.cn: 咱们是到外面吃饭还是待在家里？你决定吧。

be up to your ears in sth.lemma: be up to your ears in sth

senses.def: to have a lot of sth to deal with

ex.en: We're up to our ears in work.
ex.cn: 我们工作忙得不可开交。

be up to your eyeballs in sth.lemma: be up to your eyeballs in sth

senses.def: to have a lot of sth to deal with

ex.en: They're up to their eyeballs in work.
ex.cn: 他们的工作忙得不可开交。

be up to your eyebrows in sth.lemma: be up to your eyebrows in sth

senses.def: to have a lot of sth to deal with

ex.en: He's in it (= trouble) up to his eyebrows.
ex.cn: 他深陷于困境之中。

be up to your eyes in sth.lemma: be up to your eyes in sth

senses.def: to have a lot of sth to deal with

ex.en: We're up to our eyes in work.
ex.cn: 我们工作忙得不可开交。

be up to your neck in sth.lemma: be up to your neck in sth

senses.def: to have a lot of sth to deal with

ex.en: We're up to our neck in debt.
ex.cn: 我们债务累累。

ex.en: He's in it (= trouble) up to his neck.
ex.cn: 他遇上了麻烦，难以解脱。

senses.def: a sloping edge or surface, for example at the side of a picture frame or sheet of glass
a tool for making sloping edges on wood or stone
having a sloping edge or surface
any type of drink except water

ex.en: laws governing the sale of alcoholic beverages
ex.cn: 控制酒类销售的法规

senses.def: an alcoholic drink, especially beer

ex.en: We went out for a few bevvies last night.
ex.cn: 我们昨晚出去喝了几杯。

senses.def: a large group of people or things of the same kind
senses.chn: （同类人或东西的）一群，一批，一堆

ex.en: a bevy of beauties (= beautiful young women)
ex.cn: 一群美丽的姑娘

senses.def: to express great sadness about sth
if you tell sb to beware, you are warning them that sb/sth is dangerous and that they should be careful

ex.en: Motorists have been warned to beware of icy roads.
ex.cn: 已经提醒开车的人当心冰封的路面。

ex.en: Beware of saying anything that might reveal where you live.
ex.cn: 说话时谨防透露你的住址。

ex.en: It's a great place for swimming, but beware dangerous currents.
ex.cn: 那是个游泳的好去处，但要当心危险的水流。

senses.def: to have enough of sth

ex.en: We're well off for jobs around here (= there are many available).
ex.cn: 我们这里工作机会很多。

senses.def: to be lucky that you are not involved in sth
senses.chn: 幸运地与…无关；幸亏没有卷入

senses.def: to know a lot about sth

ex.en: He's well up in all the latest developments.
ex.cn: 他对所有的最新发展情况都了如指掌。

senses.def: wearing a wig
to confuse sb

ex.en: She was totally bewildered by his sudden change of mood.
ex.cn: 他的情绪突变搞得她全然不知所措。

senses.def: making you feel confused because there are too many things to choose from or because sth is difficult to understand
senses.chn: 令人困惑的；使人糊涂的

ex.en: a bewildering array/range
ex.cn: 令人眼花缭乱的摆设／种类

ex.en: There is a bewildering variety of software available.
ex.cn: 各种可供挑选的软件使人目不暇接。

senses.def: a feeling of being completely confused

ex.en: to look/stare in bewilderment
ex.cn: 迷惑地看着／盯着

senses.def: to understand sth, or realize what you should have done, only after sth has happened
to attract or impress sb so much that they cannot think in a sensible way

ex.en: He was completely bewitched by her beauty.
ex.cn: 他完全被她的美貌迷住了。

senses.def: to put a magic spell on sb
so beautiful or interesting that you cannot think about anything else

ex.en: a bewitching girl/smile
ex.cn: 迷人的女孩／微笑

ex.en: a bewitching performance
ex.cn: 令人陶醉的表演

senses.def: to be pregnant
to be better than anything else or anyone else of the same type

ex.en: He is a player without equal.
ex.cn: 他是个无与伦比的运动员。

senses.def: to be very active or too active

ex.en: There was nothing to worry about. It was just her imagination working overtime.
ex.cn: 没什么可担心的。那只是她的想象力太丰富了。

senses.def: to be completely different in attitudes, opinions, etc.
senses.chn: （在态度、看法等方面）有天壤之别，截然不同

be written all over sb's face.lemma: be written all over sb's face

senses.def: to be very obvious to other people from the expression on sb's face
senses.chn: 形之于色；表现得十分明显

ex.en: Guilt was written all over his face.
ex.cn: 他满脸愧疚。

senses.def: on or to the further side of sth

ex.en: The road continues beyond the village up into the hills.
ex.cn: 那条路经过村子后又往上延伸到群山中。

senses.def: later than a particular time

ex.en: It won't go on beyond midnight.
ex.cn: 这事不会延续到午夜以后。

ex.en: I know what I'll be doing for the next three weeks but I haven't thought beyond that.
ex.cn: 我知道我未来三周要干什么，但再往后我还没有想过。

senses.def: more than sth

ex.en: Our success was far beyond what we thought possible.
ex.cn: 我们的成功远远超出了我们的估计范围。

ex.en: She's got nothing beyond her state pension.
ex.cn: 除了政府发的养老金外，她什么都没有。

senses.def: used to say that sth is not possible

ex.en: The bicycle was beyond repair (= is too badly damaged to repair).
ex.cn: 自行车已损坏得无法修理。

ex.en: The situation is beyond our control.
ex.cn: 我们已无法控制这一局面。

senses.def: too far or too advanced for sb/sth

ex.en: The handle was just beyond my reach.
ex.cn: 我差一点儿才够得着把手。

ex.en: The exercise was beyond the abilities of most of the class.
ex.cn: 这个练习超出了班上大多数学生的能力。

senses.def: to be impossible for sb to imagine, understand or do
senses.chn: 使人无法想象（或理解、做等）

ex.en: It's beyond me why she wants to marry Jeff.
ex.cn: 我无法理解她为什么要嫁给杰夫。

senses.def: on the other side; further on
senses.chn: 在另一边；在（或向）更远处；以远

ex.en: Snowdon and the mountains beyond were covered in snow.
ex.cn: 斯诺登山及其以远的山脉都被积雪覆盖着。

ex.en: The immediate future is clear, but it's hard to tell what lies beyond.
ex.cn: 不久的将来已经明朗，但更往后就很难说了。

ex.en: the year 2016 and beyond
ex.cn: 2016 年及以后

ex.en: This meeting has been, without doubt, one of the most useful we have had so far.
ex.cn: 这无疑是我们迄今为止最有用的一次会议。

senses.def: (in a way that is) too great, difficult, etc. to be believed

ex.en: Dissatisfaction with the government has grown beyond belief.
ex.cn: 对政府的不满已经达到令人难以置信的程度。

ex.en: icy air that was cold beyond belief
ex.cn: 冷得令人无法相信的冰冷空气

senses.def: very much

ex.en: He irritated me beyond measure.
ex.cn: 他使我非常生气。

senses.def: extremely valuable or important
senses.chn: 无价的；极宝贵的；极重要的

senses.def: impossible to bring back to the original state; impossible to remember
senses.chn: 不可恢复；想不起来；记不住

senses.def: far more, better, etc. than you could ever have imagined or hoped for
senses.chn: 做梦都没想到；远远出乎所料；大大超出希望

senses.def: considered by most people to be unacceptable or unreasonable
senses.chn: 出格；出圈；越轨；令人不能容忍

ex.en: His remarks were clearly beyond the pale.
ex.cn: 他的话显然过分了。

senses.def: if sth is beyond your ken, you do not know enough about it to be able to understand it
senses.chn: 为某人所不理解；在某人的知识范围之外

senses.def: to be the cause of your own problems
senses.chn: 自讨苦吃；是自己问题的根源

senses.def: to act naturally

ex.en: Don't act sophisticated—just be yourself.
ex.cn: 不要装得老成持重，表现出你平常的样子就行了。

senses.def: a ring with a long narrow cut around the inside, used to hold sth in place, such as the cover of a watch or mobile/cell phone
senses.chn: （手表、手机等的）嵌玻璃凹槽，镶嵌板外圈

senses.def: a person's closest friend
(especially in text messages, emails, etc.) boyfriend; best friend
senses.chn: 男朋友，最好的朋友（全写分别为 boyfriend 和 best friend，尤用于短信、电邮等）

senses.def: (especially in text messages, emails, etc.) best friend (forever)
senses.chn: 最好的朋友，一辈子的好朋友（全写为 best friend (forever)，尤用于短信、电邮等）

ex.en: I'm going to my BFF's birthday party next week.
ex.cn: 我下星期要去参加我最好的朋友的生日聚会。

senses.def: (especially in text messages, emails, etc.) bye for now
senses.chn: 再见（全写为 bye for now，尤用于短信、电邮等）

senses.def: God

ex.en: 'May Bhagwan bless you,' he said.
ex.cn: “愿神保佑你。” 他说。

senses.def: a title for a guru or a god in the form of a man
senses.chn: 巴关（对古鲁或神的化身的称呼）

ex.en: Bhagwan Rajneesh
ex.cn: 拉吉尼希巴关大人

senses.def: a brother
used as a polite form of address to a man; in western India, often added to the first or last name
senses.chn: （对男子的礼貌称呼；在西印度，常缀于名或姓）

ex.en: Suresh Bhai
ex.cn: 苏雷什兄弟

ex.en: Gandhi Bhai
ex.cn: 甘地先生

senses.def: a spicy S Asian food consisting of vegetables fried in batter (= a mixture of flour and liquid)
senses.chn: 巴吉（南亚食品，将蔬菜放入面糊后油炸而成）

senses.def: a S Asian dish of spicy fried vegetables
the leaves and flower tops of the cannabis plant, used as a drug
senses.chn: 大麻的叶和花穗（用作麻醉品）

senses.def: a type of dance music that combines traditional Punjabi music from India and Pakistan with Western pop music
senses.chn: 彭戈拉（融合了印度和巴基斯坦的旁遮普乐和西方流行乐的舞蹈音乐）

senses.def: a classical dance form from southern India
senses.chn: 婆罗多舞（一种印度南部的古典舞）

senses.def: a building made or used for a special purpose, for example for meetings or concerts
senses.chn: （用于集会、音乐会等的）厅，馆，府

senses.def: a country in southern Asia
(a person) from Bhutan
senses.chn: 不丹人；不丹的；不丹人的

senses.def: two; twice; double

ex.en: bilingual
ex.cn: 双语的

ex.en: bicentenary
ex.cn: 两百周年

senses.def: happening twice a year
a strong feeling in favour of or against one group of people, or one side in an argument, often not based on fair judgement

ex.en: accusations of political bias in news programmes (= that reports are unfair and show favour to one political party)
ex.cn: 对新闻报道中政治倾向性的指责

ex.en: Employers must consider all candidates impartially and without bias.
ex.cn: 雇主必须公平而毫无成见地考虑所有求职者。

ex.en: Some institutions still have a strong bias against women.
ex.cn: 有些机构仍然对女性持有很大偏见。

senses.def: an interest in one thing more than others; a special ability

ex.en: The course has a strong practical bias.
ex.cn: 这个课程偏重实用。

senses.def: the fact that the results of research or an experiment are not accurate because a particular factor has not been considered when collecting the information
senses.chn: （研究或实验结果的）偏倚，偏差

ex.en: If a response rate is low, the risk of bias in the findings will be greater.
ex.cn: 如果回应率低，调查结果出现偏差的风险会增加。

senses.def: the bias of a piece of cloth is an edge cut diagonally across the threads

ex.en: The skirt is cut on the bias.
ex.cn: 这条裙子是斜裁的。

senses.def: to unfairly influence sb's opinions or decisions
senses.chn: 使有偏见；使偏心；使偏向

ex.en: The newspapers have biased people against her.
ex.cn: 报章使人们对她产生了偏见。

senses.def: to have an effect on the results of research or an experiment so that they do not show the real situation
senses.chn: 影响（研究或实验结果）以致产生偏差

ex.en: The experiment contained an error which could bias the results.
ex.cn: 这项实验有一个错误，可能导致结果出现偏差。

senses.def: cut across the natural direction of the lines in the cloth
having a tendency to show favour towards or against one group of people or one opinion for personal reasons; making unfair judgements
senses.chn: 有偏见的；倾向性的；片面的

ex.en: biased information/sources/press reports
ex.cn: 片面的信息／消息来源／新闻报道

ex.en: a biased jury/witness
ex.cn: 有成见的陪审团／证人

senses.def: having a particular interest in one thing more than others

ex.en: a school biased towards music and art
ex.cn: 一所偏重音乐和艺术的学校

senses.def: a sporting event that combines cross-country skiing and rifle shooting

ex.cn: 她一时失忆，那场事故怎么也想不起来了。

senses.def: a black powder made from dried berries (called peppercorns), used to give a spicy flavour to food

ex.en: salt and freshly ground black pepper
ex.cn: 盐和新研磨的黑胡椒粉

senses.def: a town on the coast of Lancashire in north-west England. In the past it was a popular holiday place for workers in the Lancashire cotton mills. Its famous beach is 7 miles/11 kilometres long, and the town offers a lot of entertainment. The Blackpool Tower is a famous landmark in the area. It was built in 1894 out of metal, like the Eiffel Tower in Paris, and is 520 feet/158 metres high. Blackpool is also famous for the Blackpool Illuminations, an event in the autumn when the Tower and the streets are lit up every night for several weeks with thousands of coloured lights.
senses.chn: 布莱克浦（英格兰西北部兰开夏郡沿海城镇，过去曾是兰开夏郡棉纺厂工人喜爱的度假地。其著名的海滩长 7 英里（合 11 公里）。城中有很多娱乐活动。建于 1894 年的布莱克浦塔是该地区的著名地标；像巴黎的埃菲尔铁塔一样，这座 520 英尺（合 158 米）高的塔是用金属建成的。亦因布莱克浦彩灯而闻名，这项活动在秋天举行，接连数星期布莱克浦塔和街道每晚都被数千彩灯照亮）

senses.def: a movement supporting rights and political power for black people
a type of large dark sausage made from pig's blood, fat and grain
senses.chn: 黑香肠，血肠（用猪血、油脂以及谷粒制成）

senses.def: an official who takes part in the opening ceremony of the British parliament
senses.chn: （英国议会开幕仪式上的）黑杖侍卫，黑杖礼仪官

senses.def: a person who is different from the rest of their family or another group, and who is considered bad or embarrassing
senses.chn: 有辱家族的人；害群之马

ex.en: the black sheep of the family
ex.cn: 家族败类

senses.def: a member of a fascist organization, especially in the 1920s and 30s
senses.chn: 黑衫党成员（尤指 20 世纪 20 和 30 年代的法西斯组织成员）

senses.def: a person whose job is to make and repair things made of iron, especially horseshoes
a place, a situation or an event that is a problem or that causes a lot of problems
senses.chn: 事故多发区；问题成堆的状况；（问题）焦点

ex.en: an environmental black spot
ex.cn: 环境污染严重的地区

ex.en: That corner is a notorious accident black spot (= a lot of accidents happen there).
ex.cn: 那个拐弯处是有名的事故多发区。

senses.def: a bush with thorns with black branches, white flowers and sour purple fruit called sloes
senses.chn: 黑刺李（多刺灌木，开白花，结紫色酸果）

senses.def: a black bow tie worn with a dinner jacket
a poisonous American spider. The female black widow often eats the male.
senses.chn: 黑寡妇毒蛛（美洲蜘蛛，雌蛛常吃掉雄蛛）

senses.def: an organ that is shaped like a bag in which liquid waste (= urine ) collects before it is passed out of the body
a bag made of rubber, leather, etc. that can be filled with air or liquid, such as the one inside a football
drunk
the flat part of a knife, tool or machine, which has a sharp edge or edges for cutting
one of the flat parts that turn around in an engine or on a helicopter

ex.en: the blades of a propeller
ex.cn: 螺旋桨叶

ex.en: rotor blades on a helicopter
ex.cn: 直升机的旋翼

senses.def: the flat wide part of an oar (= one of the long poles that are used to row1 a boat) that goes in the water
a single flat leaf of grass
the flat metal part on the bottom of an ice skate
the sport of moving on Rollerblades
senses.chn: 轮滑；直排轮溜冰运动；滚轴溜冰

senses.def: to persuade sb to give you sth, or to let you do sth, by talking to them in a clever or amusing way

ex.en: I blagged some tickets for the game.
ex.cn: 我骗到了这场比赛的几张门票。

ex.en: We blagged our way into the reception by saying that we were from the press.
ex.cn: 我们自称记者混进了招待会。

senses.def: people say blah, blah, blah, when they do not want to give the exact words that sb has said or written because they think they are not important or are boring
senses.chn: （觉得厌烦不想重复别人的话时说）

ex.en: They said, 'Come in, sit down, blah, blah, blah, sign here'.
ex.cn: 他们说：“进来，坐下，干这个，干那个，在这里签字。”

senses.def: not interesting

ex.en: The movie was pretty blah.
ex.cn: 那场电影真没意思。

senses.def: not feeling well; feeling slightly unhappy
to think or say that sb/sth is responsible for sth bad

ex.en: She doesn't blame anyone for her father's death.
ex.cn: 她没把她父亲的死归罪于任何人。

ex.en: A dropped cigarette is being blamed for the fire.
ex.cn: 一根乱扔的烟被认为是这场火灾的肇因。

ex.en: Police are blaming the accident on dangerous driving.
ex.cn: 警方把事故原因归咎于危险驾驶。

senses.def: to be responsible for sth bad

ex.en: If anyone's to blame, it's me.
ex.cn: 如果有人该承担责任，那就是我。

ex.en: Which driver was to blame for the accident?
ex.cn: 哪个司机是此次事故的肇事者？

senses.def: used to advise sb not to do sth, when you think they will do it despite your advice

ex.en: Call her if you like, but don't blame me if she's angry.
ex.cn: 你想给她打电话就打吧，不过要是她生气别怪我。

senses.def: used to say that you think that what sb did was reasonable and the right thing to do
senses.chn: 我不怪你（或她等）；你（或她等）的做法是可以理解的

ex.en: 'I just slammed the phone down when he said that.' 'I don't blame you!'
ex.cn: “他一说那话我就啪的一下挂了电话。” “你做得对！”

senses.def: used to say that you think sth is sb's own fault
senses.chn: 只能怪你自己；是你自己的错

ex.en: If you lose your job, you'll only have yourself to blame.
ex.cn: 如果你丢了工作，你只能怪你自己。

senses.def: responsibility for doing sth badly or wrongly; saying that sb is responsible for sth
senses.chn: （坏事或错事的）责任；责备；指责

ex.en: to lay/put the blame for sth on sb
ex.cn: 把某事归咎于某人

ex.en: The government will have to take the blame for the riots.
ex.cn: 政府将不得不对骚乱承担责任。

ex.en: Why do I always get the blame for everything that goes wrong?
ex.cn: 为什么出了事总是让我背黑锅？

senses.def: doing no wrong; free from responsibility for doing sth bad

ex.en: to lead a blameless life
ex.cn: 活得清白

ex.en: None of us is entirely blameless in this matter.
ex.cn: 在这件事上我们没有一个人是完全没有责任的。

senses.def: deserving disapproval and criticism; responsible for doing sth wrong
senses.chn: 该受指责的；（对坏事）负有责任的

senses.def: to become pale because you are shocked or frightened
to prepare food, especially vegetables, by putting it into boiling water for a short time
senses.chn: 焯（把蔬菜等放在沸水中略微一煮）

senses.def: a cold dessert (= a sweet dish) that looks like jelly, made with milk and flavoured with fruit
with little colour, excitement or interest; without anything to attract attention

ex.en: bland background music
ex.cn: 毫无情调的背景音乐

senses.def: not having a strong or interesting taste

ex.en: a rather bland diet of soup, fish and bread
ex.cn: 汤、鱼和面包的清淡饮食

senses.def: showing no strong emotions or excitement; not saying anything very interesting
senses.chn: 沉稳的；无动于衷的；讲话枯燥的

ex.en: a bland smile
ex.cn: 淡然一笑

ex.en: After the meeting, a bland statement was issued.
ex.cn: 会后发布了一条乏味的声明。

senses.def: pleasant things that you say to sb or do for them to try to persuade them to do sth
senses.chn: （因有所求而）说的好话（或做的好事），讨人欢心

senses.def: empty, with nothing written, printed or recorded on it

ex.en: Sign your name in the blank space below.
ex.cn: 把名字签在下面的空白处。

ex.en: a blank CD
ex.cn: 空白光盘

ex.en: Write on one side of the paper and leave the other side blank.
ex.cn: 写在纸的一面，把另一面空出来。

ex.en: She turned to a blank page in her notebook.
ex.cn: 她翻开笔记本的一张空白页。

senses.def: empty; with no pictures, marks or decoration
senses.chn: 空的；无图画（或标记、装饰）的

ex.en: blank whitewashed walls
ex.cn: 光秃秃的白灰墙

ex.en: Suddenly the screen went blank.
ex.cn: 屏幕突然变成一片空白。

senses.def: showing no feeling, understanding or interest
senses.chn: 没表情的；不理解的；不感兴趣的

ex.en: She stared at me with a blank expression on her face.
ex.cn: 她一脸木然地盯着我。

ex.en: Steve looked blank and said he had no idea what I was talking about.
ex.cn: 史蒂夫显得很迷惑，说他不知道我在说什么。

ex.en: Suddenly my mind went blank (= I could not remember anything).
ex.cn: 我脑子里突然一片空白。

senses.def: complete and total

ex.en: a blank refusal/denial
ex.cn: 断然拒绝／否认

senses.def: an empty space on a printed form or document for you to write answers, information, etc. in

ex.en: Please fill in the blanks.
ex.cn: 请在空白处填写。

ex.en: If you can't answer the question, leave a blank.
ex.cn: 如果回答不了问题，就空着它。

senses.def: a state of not being able to remember anything

ex.en: My mind was a blank and I couldn't remember her name.
ex.cn: 我脑子里一片空白，记不起她的名字了。

senses.def: a cartridge in a gun that contains an explosive but no bullet

ex.en: The troops fired blanks in the air.
ex.cn: 部队向天放空弹。

senses.def: to get no response or result

ex.en: So far, the police investigation has drawn a blank.
ex.cn: 到目前为止警方的调查毫无结果。

senses.def: to ignore sb completely

ex.en: I saw her on the bus this morning, but she totally blanked me.
ex.cn: 我今天早晨在公共汽车上见到她，但她连一眼都没瞧我。

senses.def: to be suddenly unable to remember or think of sth
senses.chn: 突然忘掉；突然思路模糊

ex.en: I knew the answer, but I totally blanked during the test.
ex.cn: 我本来知道答案，但考试时我什么都忘了。

senses.def: to suddenly become empty

ex.en: The screen blanked out.
ex.cn: 屏幕突然变成一片空白。

senses.def: to cover sth completely so that it cannot be seen

ex.en: All the names in the letter had been blanked out.
ex.cn: 信中所有的名字都已涂掉。

senses.def: to deliberately forget sth unpleasant

ex.en: She had tried to blank out the whole experience.
ex.cn: 她曾试图把全部经历从记忆中抹去。

senses.def: a telephone call made by a person who does not give their name and who wants to threaten, annoy or worry sb
a cheque that is signed but which does not have the amount of money to be paid written on it
senses.chn: 空白支票，空额支票（已签名但未填金额）

senses.def: permission or authority to do sth that is necessary in a particular situation

ex.en: The President was given a blank check by Congress to continue the war.
ex.cn: 国会授予总统全权可继续这场战争。

senses.def: a large cover, often made of wool, used especially on beds to keep people warm
a thick layer or covering of sth

ex.en: a blanket of fog/snow/cloud
ex.cn: 厚厚的一层雾／雪／云

ex.en: The trial was conducted under a blanket of secrecy.
ex.cn: 审讯在高度保密下进行。

senses.def: including or affecting all possible cases, situations or people
senses.chn: 包括所有情形（或人员）的；总括的；综合的

ex.en: a blanket ban on tobacco advertising
ex.cn: 烟草广告的全面取缔

ex.en: a blanket refusal
ex.cn: 完全拒绝

senses.def: to cover sth completely with a thick layer

ex.en: The ground was soon blanketed with snow.
ex.cn: 地面很快铺上了一层厚厚的积雪。

senses.def: an act of washing the whole of sb's body when they cannot get out of bed because they are sick, injured or old
senses.chn: （为伤病或年老者所做的）卧床浴，卧床全身擦浴

senses.def: to suddenly become empty

ex.en: The screen blanked out.
ex.cn: 屏幕突然变成一片空白。

senses.def: poetry that has a regular rhythm, usually with ten syllables and five stresses in each line, but which does not rhyme
senses.chn: 无韵诗（不押韵的抑扬五音步诗行，常为每行十个音节）

senses.def: to make a loud unpleasant noise
senses.chn: 发出响亮而刺耳的声音

ex.en: police cars with lights flashing and sirens blaring
ex.cn: 警灯闪烁、警笛刺耳的警车

ex.en: Music blared out from the open window.
ex.cn: 喧闹的音乐从敞开的窗口传出。

ex.en: The radio was blaring (out) rock music.
ex.cn: 收音机在高声播放着嘈杂的摇滚乐。

senses.def: a loud unpleasant noise

ex.en: the blare of car horns
ex.cn: 汽车喇叭的刺耳声

senses.def: talk that is friendly and amusing but probably not true, and which may be used to persuade or trick you
to speak about God or the holy things of a particular religion in an offensive way; to swear using the names of God or holy things
behaviour or language that insults or shows a lack of respect for God or religion
senses.chn: 亵渎上帝（或神明）的言行

senses.def: an explosion or a powerful movement of air caused by an explosion
senses.chn: 爆炸；（爆炸引起的）气浪，冲击波

ex.en: a bomb blast
ex.cn: 炸弹爆炸

ex.en: 27 schoolchildren were injured in the blast.
ex.cn: 27 名学龄儿童在爆炸中受了伤。

senses.def: a sudden strong movement of air

ex.en: A blast of hot air hit us as we stepped off the plane.
ex.cn: 我们下飞机时，一股热浪向我们袭来。

ex.en: the wind's icy blasts
ex.cn: 凛冽的狂风

senses.def: a sudden loud noise, especially one made by a musical instrument that you blow, or by a whistle or a car horn
senses.chn: （吹奏乐器、哨子、汽车喇叭等突然发出的）响声，吹奏声，轰鸣

ex.en: three short blasts on the ship's siren
ex.cn: 船上三次短促的汽笛声

senses.def: strong criticism
senses.chn: 严厉的批评；激烈的抨击

ex.en: Blast for prison governors in judge's report.
ex.cn: 法官报告中对典狱长猛烈抨击

senses.def: a very enjoyable experience that is a lot of fun

ex.en: The party was a blast.
ex.cn: 聚会非常热闹。

ex.en: We had a blast at the party.
ex.cn: 我们在聚会上玩得很开心。

senses.def: a piece of advertising or information that is sent to a large number of people at the same time by email
senses.chn: 群发的电子邮件广告（或信息）

senses.def: a person or thing from your past that you see, hear, meet, etc. again in the present
senses.chn: （现在又看见、听到、遇到等的）故人，往事，旧物

senses.def: with the greatest possible volume or power
senses.chn: 最大音量地；最大马力地

ex.en: She had the car stereo on at full blast.
ex.cn: 她把汽车音响开到了最大音量。

senses.def: to violently destroy or break sth into pieces, using explosives
senses.chn: （用炸药）炸毁，把…炸成碎片；爆破

ex.en: They blasted a huge crater in the runway.
ex.cn: 他们在飞机跑道上炸了一个大坑。

ex.en: They had to blast a tunnel through the mountain.
ex.cn: 他们得炸出一条穿山隧道。

ex.en: All the windows were blasted inwards with the force of the explosion.
ex.cn: 爆炸的震动力把所有窗户都震碎到屋里。

ex.en: The jumbo jet was blasted out of the sky.
ex.cn: 那架巨型喷气式飞机在空中被炸成碎片。

ex.en: Danger! Blasting in Progress!
ex.cn: 危险！爆破进行中！

senses.def: to make a loud unpleasant noise, especially music
senses.chn: 发出刺耳的高音，轰鸣（尤指音乐）

ex.en: Music suddenly blasted out from the speakers.
ex.cn: 喇叭中突然响起了轰鸣的音乐。

ex.en: The radio blasted out rock music at full volume.
ex.cn: 收音机以最大音量播放摇滚乐。

senses.def: to criticize sb/sth severely

ex.en: The movie was blasted by all the critics.
ex.cn: 这部影片受到了所有评论家的严厉抨击。

senses.def: to hit, kick or shoot sb/sth with a lot of force

ex.en: He blasted the ball past the goalie.
ex.cn: 他飞脚将球踢过了守门员。

ex.en: He blasted (= shot) the policeman right between the eyes.
ex.cn: 他对着那个警察的眉心开了一枪。

senses.def: to direct air, water, etc. at sb/sth with a lot of force

ex.en: Police blasted the demonstrators with water cannons.
ex.cn: 警察用高压水炮喷射示威者。

senses.def: to destroy sth such as a plant with disease, cold, heat, etc.
senses.chn: 使（植物等）毁于疾病（或寒冷、酷热等）

ex.en: Their whole crop had been blasted by a late frost.
ex.cn: 一场晚霜把他们的庄稼全毁了。

senses.def: if a gun or sb using a gun blasts away, the gun fires continuously and loudly
to leave the ground
people sometimes say Blast! when they are annoyed about sth

ex.en: Oh blast! The car won't start.
ex.cn: 真该死！车子发动不了。

senses.def: if a gun or sb using a gun blasts away, the gun fires continuously and loudly
used when you are very annoyed about sth
senses.chn: （十分恼火时说）该死的，可恶的

ex.en: Make your own blasted coffee!
ex.cn: 你自己煮那该死的咖啡吧！

senses.def: a large structure like an oven in which iron ore (= rock containing iron) is melted in order to take out the metal
to leave the ground
the moment when a spacecraft leaves the ground
done in an obvious and open way without caring if people are shocked

ex.en: a blatant attempt to buy votes
ex.cn: 公然的贿选企图

ex.en: It was a blatant lie.
ex.cn: 那是个赤裸裸的谎言。

senses.def: to talk continuously about things that are silly or unimportant
the use of black people in films/movies, especially in a way which shows them in fixed ways that are different from real life
senses.chn: 黑人利用（尤指在电影中黑人形象模式化且脱离现实）

senses.def: to burn brightly and strongly

ex.en: A huge fire was blazing in the fireplace.
ex.cn: 壁炉中火烧得正旺。

ex.en: Within minutes the whole building was blazing.
ex.cn: 不消几分钟整个大楼便成了一片火海。

ex.en: He rushed back into the blazing house.
ex.cn: 他又冲进了燃烧着的房子。

senses.def: to shine brightly

ex.en: The sun blazed down from a clear blue sky.
ex.cn: 耀眼的阳光从清澈蔚蓝的天空中照射下来。

ex.en: The garden blazed with colour.
ex.cn: 花园里姹紫嫣红。

senses.def: if sb's eyes blaze, they look extremely angry

ex.en: Her eyes were blazing with fury.
ex.cn: 她的双眼燃烧着怒火。

senses.def: to make news or information widely known by telling people about it in a way they are sure to notice

ex.en: The story was blazed all over the daily papers.
ex.cn: 那个传闻被各家报纸炒得沸沸扬扬。

senses.def: if a gun or sb using a gun blazes, the gun fires continuously

ex.en: In the distance machine guns were blazing.
ex.cn: 机关枪在远处不停地射击。

senses.def: to be the first to do or to discover sth that others follow

ex.en: The department is blazing a trail in the field of laser surgery.
ex.cn: 这个部门正在为激光外科学领域开辟一条新路。

senses.def: with a lot of energy and determination

ex.en: The champions came out (with) all guns blazing.
ex.cn: 优胜者们神采奕奕地登场亮相。

senses.def: to suddenly start burning very strongly
to suddenly become very angry
a very large fire, especially a dangerous one

ex.en: Five people died in the blaze.
ex.cn: 火灾中有五人丧生。

senses.def: strong bright flames in a fire

ex.en: Dry wood makes a good blaze.
ex.cn: 干木柴烧得旺。

senses.def: a very bright show of lights or colour; an impressive or noticeable show of sth

ex.en: The gardens are a blaze of colour.
ex.cn: 花园里姹紫嫣红。

ex.en: a blaze of lights in the city centre
ex.cn: 市中心通明的灯火

ex.en: the bright blaze of the sun
ex.cn: 太阳的光辉

ex.en: a blaze of glory
ex.cn: 荣耀

ex.en: They got married in a blaze of publicity.
ex.cn: 他们结婚的事受到了传媒的广泛关注。

senses.def: a sudden show of very strong feeling

ex.en: a blaze of anger/passion/hate
ex.cn: 怒火／激情／仇恨的迸发

senses.def: a white mark on an animal's face
used to emphasize that you are annoyed and surprised, to avoid using the word 'hell'
senses.chn: （委婉语，烦恼和惊奇时说，与 hell 同义）

ex.en: What the blazes have you done?
ex.cn: 你到底搞的什么名堂？

senses.def: very hard; very fast
to be the first to do or to discover sth that others follow

ex.en: The department is blazing a trail in the field of laser surgery.
ex.cn: 这个部门正在为激光外科学领域开辟一条新路。

senses.def: a jacket, not worn with matching trousers/pants, often showing the colours or badge of a club, school, team, etc.
senses.chn: （常带有俱乐部、学校、运动队等的颜色或徽章的）夹克

senses.def: to suddenly start burning very strongly
to suddenly become very angry
extremely hot

ex.en: blazing heat
ex.cn: 十分炎热

ex.cn: 他在强烈的阳光下直眨眼睛。

ex.cn: 我眨眼工夫就回来。

ex.cn: 我把那个消息告诉他时，他眼都没眨一下。

ex.en: Suddenly a warning light blinked.
ex.cn: 突然有一盏警告灯开始闪亮。

senses.def: to try to control tears or clear your eyes by blinking
senses.chn: 眨眼以控制泪水（或挤掉脏东西）

ex.cn: 她勇敢地抑制住了泪水。

no longer working correctly

ex.cn: 我们应该用新的眼光全面地考虑这个计划。

ex.cn: 我们无忧无虑地度了三个星期的假。

senses.def: a failure to do sth that must be done by law

ex.en: a breach of contract/copyright/warranty
ex.cn: 违约；侵犯版权；违反保证

ex.en: They are in breach of Article 119.
ex.cn: 他们违犯了第 119 条。

ex.en: (a) breach of the peace (= the crime of behaving in a noisy or violent way in public)
ex.cn: 扰乱治安

senses.def: an action that breaks an agreement to behave in a particular way

ex.en: a breach of confidence/trust
ex.cn: 泄密；背信

ex.en: a breach of security (= when sth that is normally protected is no longer secure)
ex.cn: 破坏安全

senses.def: a break in a relationship between people or countries

ex.en: a breach in Franco-German relations
ex.cn: 法德关系的破裂

senses.def: an opening that is created during a military attack or by strong winds or seas

ex.en: They escaped through a breach in the wire fence.
ex.cn: 他们从铁丝网上的一个缺口逃走了。

senses.def: to do sb's job or work when they are suddenly or unexpectedly unable to do it
senses.chn: 临时顶替某人工作；临时顶缺

senses.def: to not keep to an agreement or not keep a promise

ex.en: The government is accused of breaching the terms of the treaty.
ex.cn: 政府被控违反条约中的规定。

senses.def: to make a hole in a wall, fence, etc. so that sb/sth can go through it

ex.en: The dam had been breached.
ex.cn: 大坝决口了。

senses.def: a type of food made from flour, water and usually yeast mixed together and baked

ex.en: a loaf/slice/piece of bread
ex.cn: 一条／一片／一块面包

ex.en: white/brown/wholemeal bread
ex.cn: 白／黑／全麦面包

senses.def: money
to take away sb's job so that they are no longer able to earn enough money to live
senses.chn: 剥夺某人的生计；砸某人的饭碗

senses.def: the basic things that you need to live, especially food
you should be grateful for sth, even if it is not as good, much, etc. as you really wanted; something is better than nothing
senses.chn: 半块面包比没有面包强；聊胜于无

senses.def: to know where you can get an advantage for yourself
if you say that sth is the best thing since sliced bread, you think it is extremely good, interesting, etc.
senses.chn: 极好（或极有意思等）的事物

senses.def: slices of bread that have been spread with butter

ex.en: a piece of bread and butter
ex.cn: 一块黄油面包

senses.def: a person or company's main source of income
senses.chn: （某人或公司的）主要收入来源

senses.def: basic; very important

ex.en: Employment and taxation are the bread-and-butter issues of politics.
ex.cn: 就业和征税是很重要的政治问题。

senses.def: a dessert (= sweet dish) consisting of layers of bread with butter on, cooked with dried fruit in a mixture of eggs and milk
senses.chn: 面包黄油布丁，面包奶油布丁（黄油面包层加干果在鸡蛋牛奶中烘焙而成）

senses.def: the part of a country or region that produces large amounts of food, especially grain, for the rest of the country or region
senses.chn: 粮仓（指一国或地区的粮食生产基地，尤指谷物生产基地）

senses.def: a wooden, metal or plastic container for keeping bread in so that it stays fresh
a flat board used for cutting bread on
very small pieces of bread that can be used in cooking
a series of links displayed at the top of a web page, indicating the path to that page
senses.chn: 面包屑导航（网页上方指向该页面的路径链接信息）

senses.def: covered in breadcrumbs
a large tropical fruit with a thick skin, that tastes and feels like bread when it is cooked. It grows on a tree which is called a breadfruit tree.
senses.chn: 面包果（皮厚个大，煮熟似面包）

senses.def: the lowest level of income on which it is possible to live
senses.chn: 只能勉强维持生计的收入水平；贫困线

ex.en: Many people without jobs are living on the breadline (= are very poor).
ex.cn: 很多没工作的人生活十分贫苦。

senses.def: (in the past) a line of people waiting to receive free food
senses.chn: （旧时）等待领取救济食品的队伍

senses.def: a heavy cake or dessert (= sweet dish) made by pouring eggs and milk over bread and then cooking it with dried fruit and sugar
senses.chn: 面包布丁（在面包上加蛋、奶、果干和糖烹制而成）

senses.def: a long thin piece of bread, which is dry like a biscuit
a piece of fresh bread, baked in the shape of a small stick
the distance or measurement from one side to the other; how broad or wide sth is

ex.en: She estimated the breadth of the lake to be 500 metres.
ex.cn: 她估计湖面大约有 500 米宽。

senses.def: a wide range (of knowledge, interests, etc.)

ex.en: He was surprised at her breadth of reading.
ex.cn: 他对于她的博览群书感到惊讶。

ex.en: The curriculum needs breadth and balance.
ex.cn: 课程设置应该内容广泛而且均衡。

ex.en: a new political leader whose breadth of vision (= willingness to accept new ideas) can persuade others to change
ex.cn: 一位能凭远见卓识说服他人做出改变的新政治领袖

senses.def: in or to all parts of a place

ex.en: They have travelled the length and breadth of Europe giving concerts.
ex.cn: 他们为举行音乐会走遍了欧洲各地。

senses.def: a large plant found in tropical and southern Africa whose thick main stem can be made into a type of flour
senses.chn: 面包棕榈（产于非洲南部，树干可制成面粉）

senses.def: a person who supports their family with the money they earn
to be damaged and separated into two or more parts , as a result of force; to damage sth in this way

ex.en: All the windows broke with the force of the blast.
ex.cn: 爆炸的巨大力量震碎了所有的窗户。

ex.en: She dropped the plate and it broke into pieces.
ex.cn: 她把盘子掉在地上打碎了。

ex.en: to break a cup/window
ex.cn: 打破杯子／窗户

ex.en: She fell off a ladder and broke her arm.
ex.cn: 她从梯子上掉下来，摔断了胳膊。

ex.en: He broke the chocolate in two.
ex.cn: 他把那块巧克力一分为二。

ex.en: The balloon hit a tree and burst.
ex.cn: 气球碰到树就爆了。

senses.def: to stop working as a result of being damaged; to damage sth and stop it from working

ex.en: My watch has broken.
ex.cn: 我的表坏了。

ex.en: I think I've broken the washing machine.
ex.cn: 我可能把洗衣机弄坏了。

senses.def: to cut the surface of the skin and make it bleed

ex.en: The dog bit me but didn't break the skin.
ex.cn: 那条狗咬了我，但没咬破皮肤。

senses.def: to do sth that is against the law; to not keep a promise, etc.

ex.en: to break the law/rules/conditions
ex.cn: 违反法律／规章／所定条件

ex.en: to break an agreement/a contract/a promise/your word
ex.cn: 违反协议／合同／允诺；食言

ex.en: to break an appointment (= not to come to it)
ex.cn: 失约

ex.en: He was breaking the speed limit (= travelling faster than the law allows).
ex.cn: 他违章超速驾驶。

senses.def: to stop doing sth for a while, especially when it is time to eat or have a drink

ex.en: Let's break for lunch.
ex.cn: 我们休息一会儿，吃午饭。

ex.en: a broken night's sleep (= a night during which you often wake up)
ex.cn: 夜间时时醒来的睡眠

ex.en: We broke our journey in Oxford (= stopped in Oxford on the way to the place we were going to).
ex.cn: 我们途中在牛津停留了一下。

senses.def: to interrupt sth so that it ends suddenly

ex.en: She broke the silence by coughing.
ex.cn: 她的咳嗽声打破了寂静。

ex.en: A tree broke his fall (= stopped him as he was falling).
ex.cn: 他坠落时一棵树挡住了他。

ex.en: The phone rang and broke my train of thought.
ex.cn: 电话铃响起来，打断了我的思路。

senses.def: to make sth end by using force or strong action

ex.en: an attempt to break the year-long siege
ex.cn: 试图冲破长达一年的围困

ex.en: Management has not succeeded in breaking the strike.
ex.cn: 资方未能使罢工终止。

senses.def: to end a connection with sth or a relationship with sb

ex.en: He broke all ties with his parents.
ex.cn: 他断绝了与父母的一切关系。

senses.def: to get away from or out of a position in which they are stuck or trapped

ex.en: He finally managed to break free from his attacker.
ex.cn: 他终于设法逃脱了袭击他的人。

senses.def: to destroy sth or make sb/sth weaker; to become weak or be destroyed

ex.en: to break sb's morale/resistance/resolve/spirit
ex.cn: 瓦解某人的士气／抵抗／决心／精神

ex.en: The government was determined to break the power of the trade unions.
ex.cn: 政府决心削弱工会的力量。

ex.en: The scandal broke him (= ruined his reputation and destroyed his confidence).
ex.cn: 这桩丑闻把他毁了。

ex.en: She broke under questioning (= was no longer able to bear it) and confessed to everything.
ex.cn: 她经不住盘问，招认了一切。

senses.def: to make sb feel so sad, lonely, etc. that they cannot live a normal life
senses.chn: 使心碎；使十分悲伤；使孤寂

ex.en: The death of his wife broke him completely.
ex.cn: 妻子的死使他悲痛欲绝。

senses.def: to change suddenly, usually after a period when it has been fine
to show an opening

ex.en: The clouds broke and the sun came out.
ex.cn: 云开日出。

senses.def: when the day or dawn or a storm breaks, it begins

ex.en: Dawn was breaking when they finally left.
ex.cn: 他们终于离开时正是破晓时分。

senses.def: if a piece of news breaks, it becomes known

ex.en: There was a public outcry when the scandal broke.
ex.cn: 丑闻一传开，舆论一片哗然。

ex.en: breaking news (= news that is arriving about events that have just happened)
ex.cn: 突发性新闻

senses.def: to be the first to tell sb some bad news
senses.chn: （第一个将坏消息向某人）公布，透露，说出

ex.en: Who's going to break it to her?
ex.cn: 由谁来把这事告诉她呢？

ex.en: I'm sorry to be the one to break the news to you.
ex.cn: 我很难过，这消息得由我来告诉你。

senses.def: if sb's voice breaks, it changes its tone because of emotion

ex.en: Her voice broke as she told us the dreadful news.
ex.cn: 她告诉我们这可怕的消息时，声音都变了。

senses.def: when a boy's voice breaks, it becomes permanently deeper at about the age of 13 or 14
senses.chn: （指男孩在 13 或 14 岁时嗓音）变粗，变低

senses.def: to do sth better, faster, etc. than anyone has ever done it before

ex.en: She had broken the world 100 metres record.
ex.cn: 她打破了 100 米世界纪录。

ex.en: The movie broke all box-office records.
ex.cn: 这部影片打破了所有的票房纪录。

senses.def: when waves break, they fall and are dissolved into foam, usually near land

ex.en: the sound of waves breaking on the beach
ex.cn: 浪涛拍岸的声音

ex.en: The sea was breaking over the wrecked ship.
ex.cn: 海浪冲刷着破船的残骸。

senses.def: to find the meaning of sth secret

ex.en: to break a code
ex.cn: 破译密码

senses.def: to change a banknote for coins

ex.en: Can you break a twenty-dollar bill?
ex.cn: 可以给我找开二十美元的钞票吗？

senses.def: to escape suddenly from sb who is holding you or keeping you prisoner

ex.en: The prisoner broke away from his guards.
ex.cn: 犯人挣脱了看守。

senses.def: to leave a political party, state, etc., especially to form a new one
senses.chn: 脱离，背叛（政党、国家等，尤指为了组建新的）

ex.en: The people of the province wished to break away and form a new state.
ex.cn: 该省人民希望分离成立一个新国家。

senses.def: to move away from a crowd or group, especially in a race

ex.en: She broke away from the pack and opened up a two-second lead.
ex.cn: 她甩开所有其他赛跑者，以两秒领先。

senses.def: to stop working because of a fault

ex.en: The telephone system has broken down.
ex.cn: 电话系统瘫痪了。

ex.en: We (= the car) broke down on the freeway.
ex.cn: 我们的车在高速公路上抛锚了。

senses.def: to fail

ex.en: Negotiations between the two sides have broken down.
ex.cn: 双方谈判失败了。

senses.def: to become very bad

ex.en: Her health broke down under the pressure of work.
ex.cn: 她因工作压力身体垮掉了。

senses.def: to lose control of your feelings and start crying

ex.en: He broke down and wept when he heard the news.
ex.cn: 听到这个消息，他不禁失声痛哭。

senses.def: to divide into parts to be analysed

ex.en: Expenditure on the project breaks down as follows: wages $10m, plant $4m, raw materials $5m.
ex.cn: 这项工程的支出费用分项列明如下：工资 1 000 万美元，设备 400 万美元，原料 500 万美元。

senses.def: to make sth fall down, open, etc. by hitting it hard

ex.en: Firefighters had to break the door down to reach the people trapped inside.
ex.cn: 消防队员不得不破门而入，解救困在里面的人。

senses.def: to destroy sth or make it disappear, especially a particular feeling or attitude that sb has
senses.chn: 破坏，消除（尤指某种感情或态度）

ex.en: to break down resistance/opposition
ex.cn: 瓦解抵抗／反对

ex.en: to break down sb's reserve/shyness
ex.cn: 驱除某人的矜持／胆怯

ex.en: Attempts must be made to break down the barriers of fear and hostility which divide the two communities.
ex.cn: 必须设法消除造成这两个团体不和的恐惧和敌意。

senses.def: to divide sth into parts in order to analyse it or make it easier to do

ex.en: Break your expenditure down into bills, food and other.
ex.cn: 把支出费用按账单、食物及其他分类列明。

ex.en: Each lesson is broken down into several units.
ex.cn: 每一课都分成几个单元。

senses.def: to make a substance separate into parts or change into a different form in a chemical process

ex.en: Sugar and starch are broken down in the stomach.
ex.cn: 糖和淀粉在胃里被分解。

senses.def: to suddenly run towards sth when you are trying to escape
senses.chn: （试图逃脱时）突然冲向；向…挣脱

ex.en: She had to hold him back as he tried to break for the door.
ex.cn: 他试图向门口逃去，她只好拉住他。

senses.def: to enter a building by force

ex.en: Burglars had broken in while we were away.
ex.cn: 我们不在家时，窃贼闯进屋里了。

senses.def: to train sb/sth in sth new that they must do

ex.en: to break in new recruits
ex.cn: 训练新人

ex.en: The young horse was not yet broken in (= trained to carry a rider).
ex.cn: 那匹刚长成的马还没被驯服。

senses.def: to wear sth, especially new shoes, until they become comfortable
senses.chn: 把…穿得合身，使舒适自如（尤指新鞋）

senses.def: to interrupt or disturb sth

ex.en: She longed to break in on their conversation but didn't want to appear rude.
ex.cn: 她很想打断他们的谈话，但又不愿显得粗鲁。

ex.en: 'I didn't do it!' she broke in.
ex.cn: “不是我干的！” 她插嘴说。

senses.def: to enter a building by force; to open a car, etc. by force

ex.en: We had our car broken into last week.
ex.cn: 我们的车上周被撬了。

senses.def: to begin laughing, singing, etc. suddenly

ex.en: As the President's car drew up, the crowd broke into loud applause.
ex.cn: 总统的座驾停下时，人群中爆发出热烈的掌声。

senses.def: to suddenly start running; to start running faster than before

ex.en: He broke into a run when he saw the police.
ex.cn: 他看见警察，撒腿就跑。

ex.en: Her horse broke into a trot.
ex.cn: 她的马突然开始加速小跑。

senses.def: to use a banknote of high value to buy sth that costs less
senses.chn: 找开（大面值钞票买小额商品）

ex.en: I had to break into a £20 note to pay the bus fare.
ex.cn: 我只好找开一张 20 英镑的钞票买公交车票。

senses.def: to open and use sth that has been kept for an emergency

ex.en: They had to break into the emergency food supplies.
ex.cn: 他们不得不动用应急食物。

senses.def: to be successful when you get involved in sth

ex.en: The company is having difficulty breaking into new markets.
ex.cn: 该公司在打入新市场时遇到困难。

senses.def: to become separated from sth as a result of force

ex.en: The back section of the plane had broken off.
ex.cn: 飞机尾部脱落了。

senses.def: to stop speaking or stop doing sth for a time

ex.en: He broke off in the middle of a sentence.
ex.cn: 他一句话说了一半就不说了。

senses.def: to separate sth, using force

ex.en: She broke off a piece of chocolate and gave it to me.
ex.cn: 她掰了一块巧克力给我。

senses.def: to end sth suddenly

ex.en: Britain threatened to break off diplomatic relations.
ex.cn: 英国威胁说要断绝外交关系。

ex.en: They've broken off their engagement.
ex.cn: 他们突然解除了婚约。

senses.def: to start suddenly

ex.en: They had escaped to America shortly before war broke out in 1939.
ex.cn: 1939 年战争爆发前不久他们逃到了美国。

ex.en: Fighting had broken out between rival groups of fans.
ex.cn: 双方球迷发生了打斗。

ex.en: Fire broke out during the night.
ex.cn: 夜间突然发生了火灾。

senses.def: to escape from a place or situation

ex.en: Several prisoners broke out of the jail.
ex.cn: 几名囚犯越狱了。

ex.en: She needed to break out of her daily routine and do something exciting.
ex.cn: 她需要从日常事务中解脱出来，找点有意思的事做。

senses.def: to suddenly become covered in sth

ex.en: Her face broke out in a rash.
ex.cn: 她脸上突然长出一片红疹。

ex.en: He broke out in a cold sweat (= for example, through fear).
ex.cn: 他突然冒出一身冷汗。

senses.def: to make new and important discoveries

ex.en: Scientists think they are beginning to break through in the fight against cancer.
ex.cn: 科学家认为他们在对抗癌症的研究中开始有所突破。

senses.def: to make a way through sth using force

ex.en: Demonstrators broke through the police cordon.
ex.cn: 示威群众冲破了警方的警戒线。

senses.def: to appear from behind clouds

ex.en: The sun broke through at last in the afternoon.
ex.cn: 下午太阳终于拨云而出。

senses.def: to succeed in dealing with an attitude that sb has and the difficulties it creates

ex.en: He had finally managed to break through her reserve.
ex.cn: 他终于设法消除了她的拘谨。

senses.def: to separate into smaller pieces

ex.en: The ship broke up on the rocks.
ex.cn: 船触礁撞碎了。

senses.def: to come to an end

ex.en: Their marriage has broken up.
ex.cn: 他们的婚姻已经破裂。

senses.def: to go away in different directions

ex.en: The meeting broke up at eleven o'clock.
ex.cn: 会议在十一点散会。

senses.def: to begin the holidays when school closes at the end of a term

ex.en: When do you break up for Christmas?
ex.cn: 你们什么时候放假过圣诞节？

senses.def: to become very weak

ex.en: He was breaking up under the strain.
ex.cn: 过度的劳累使他快要垮了。

senses.def: to laugh very hard

ex.en: Woody Allen makes me just break up.
ex.cn: 伍迪 · 艾伦令我几乎笑破肚皮。

senses.def: when a person who is talking on a mobile/cell phone breaks up, you can no longer hear them clearly because the signal has been interrupted
senses.chn: （打移动电话的人）声音不清（因信号受干扰）

senses.def: to make sb feel upset

ex.en: The thought of hurting her just breaks me up.
ex.cn: 一想到要伤害她我就感到不安。

senses.def: to make sth separate into smaller pieces; to divide sth into smaller parts

ex.en: The ship was broken up for scrap metal.
ex.cn: 船被拆解成为废铁。

ex.en: Sentences can be broken up into clauses.
ex.cn: 句子可以分成从句。

senses.def: to end a relationship, a company, etc.

ex.en: They decided to break up the partnership.
ex.cn: 他们决定拆伙。

senses.def: to make people leave sth or stop doing sth, especially by using force

ex.en: Police were called in to break up the fight.
ex.cn: 有人叫来了警察制止打斗。

senses.def: to end a relationship with sb

ex.en: She's just broken up with her boyfriend.
ex.cn: 她刚刚和男朋友分手。

senses.def: to end a connection with sth

ex.en: to break with tradition/old habits/the past
ex.cn: 摒弃传统／旧习惯／过去

senses.def: a short period of time when you stop what you are doing and rest, eat, etc.

ex.en: a coffee/lunch/tea break
ex.cn: 用咖啡／午饭／茶的休息时间

ex.en: Let's take a break.
ex.cn: 咱们休息会儿吧。

ex.en: a break for lunch
ex.cn: 午餐休息

ex.en: She worked all day without a break.
ex.cn: 她接连工作了一整天。

ex.en: We stopped for a well-earned rest.
ex.cn: 我们停下来作个应有的休息。

ex.en: Let's take a break.
ex.cn: 咱们休息一会儿吧。

senses.def: a period of time between lessons at school

ex.en: Come and see me at break.
ex.cn: 课间休息时来见我。

senses.def: a pause or period of time when sth stops before starting again

ex.en: a break in my daily routine
ex.cn: 我日常生活中的一段小插曲

ex.en: She wanted to take a career break in order to have children.
ex.cn: 她想暂时放下工作，去生孩子。

senses.def: a pause for advertisements in the middle of a television or radio programme
senses.chn: （电视或电台节目的）插播广告的间隙

ex.en: More news after the break.
ex.cn: 广告后继续报道新闻。

senses.def: a short holiday/vacation

ex.en: We had a weekend break in New York.
ex.cn: 我们在纽约度过了一个周末假日。

ex.en: a well-earned break
ex.cn: 应得的休假

senses.def: the moment when a situation or a relationship that has existed for a time changes, ends or is interrupted
senses.chn: （持续一段时间的状况或关系的）改变，终止，中断

ex.cn: 外交关系的中断

ex.cn: X 光照片显示他的腿没有骨折。

ex.cn: 这是本盘比赛中她第二次破掉对手的发球局。

senses.def: the moment in the early hours of the morning when it begins to get light

ex.cn: 别苛求这小伙子，他上工才第二天。

senses.def: to run towards sth in order to try and escape

ex.en: He suddenly leapt up and made a break for the door.
ex.cn: 他突然一跃而起，向门口逃窜。

ex.cn: 他们决定那天晚上逃跑。

senses.def: a complete separation from a person, an organization, a way of life, etc.

senses.def: a break in a bone in one place
likely to break; easily broken
an object that has been broken

ex.cn: 我们上次搬家时几乎没有什么物品破损。

senses.def: the act of breaking sth

ex.cn: 脱离原组织的派系／集体／部分

ex.cn: 对他以往演唱风格的改变

senses.def: a style of dancing with acrobatic movements, often performed in the street
senses.chn: 霹雳舞（掺入杂技动作，常在街头表演）

senses.def: an occasion when a vehicle or machine stops working

ex.cn: 在高速公路上出的故障

ex.en: a breakdown recovery service
ex.cn: 车辆抢修服务

senses.def: a failure of a relationship, discussion or system

ex.cn: 婚姻破裂

ex.en: marriage breakdown
ex.cn: 婚姻破裂

ex.en: a breakdown in communications
ex.cn: 通信中断

ex.cn: 谈判的失败是预料之中的事。

ex.cn: 治安陷入瘫痪

ex.cn: 我们首先看一下成本的详细数字。

ex.cn: 蛋白质在消化系统中的分解

ex.cn: 电话系统瘫痪了。

ex.cn: 我们的车在高速公路上抛锚了。

ex.cn: 双方谈判失败了。

ex.cn: 她因工作压力身体垮掉了。

ex.cn: 听到这个消息，他不禁失声痛哭。

ex.cn: 这项工程的支出费用分项列明如下：工资 1 000 万美元，设备 400 万美元，原料 500 万美元。

senses.chn: 硬路肩（在高速公路旁，可供紧急停车）

senses.def: a truck that is used for taking cars away to be repaired when they have had a breakdown
senses.chn: （把故障车辆送去修理的）救险车

senses.def: a large wave covered with white bubbles that is moving towards land

ex.cn: 这家公司去年接近收支平衡。

senses.def: a time when a company or piece of business earns just enough money to pay for its costs

ex.cn: 公司预期明年达到盈亏平衡。

senses.def: the first meal of the day

ex.en: a big/hearty/light breakfast
ex.cn: 量大的／丰盛的／量少的早餐

ex.en: a cooked breakfast
ex.cn: 热食早餐

ex.en: Do you want bacon and eggs for breakfast?
ex.cn: 你早饭要吃熏咸肉和鸡蛋吗？

ex.en: They were having breakfast when I arrived.
ex.cn: 我到达时他们正在吃早饭。

ex.en: She doesn't eat much breakfast.
ex.cn: 她早饭吃得不多。

ex.en: He's made a real dog's breakfast of these accounts.
ex.cn: 他把这些账目搞得简直一塌糊涂。

senses.def: to eat breakfast

ex.en: She had to hold him back as he tried to break for the door.
ex.cn: 他试图向门口逃去，她只好拉住他。

senses.def: to enter a building by force

ex.en: Burglars had broken in while we were away.
ex.cn: 我们不在家时，窃贼闯进屋里了。

senses.def: an entry into a building using force, usually to steal sth
senses.chn: 破门而入；闯入；入室偷窃

ex.cn: 已抻至极限

ex.cn: 我们的车上周被撬了。

ex.cn: 总统的座驾停下时，人群中爆发出热烈的掌声。

ex.cn: 他看见警察，撒腿就跑。

ex.cn: 她的马突然开始加速小跑。

senses.chn: 找开（大面值钞票买小额商品）

ex.cn: 我只好找开一张 20 英镑的钞票买公交车票。

senses.def: to open and use sth that has been kept for an emergency

ex.en: They had to break into the emergency food supplies.
ex.cn: 他们不得不动用应急食物。

senses.def: to be successful when you get involved in sth

ex.cn: 该公司在打入新市场时遇到困难。

senses.def: very fast and dangerous

ex.en: to drive, etc. at breakneck speed
ex.cn: 亡命飞车等

senses.def: to make a new discovery or do sth that has not been done before

ex.cn: 飞机尾部脱落了。

ex.en: He broke off in the middle of a sentence.
ex.cn: 他一句话说了一半就不说了。

ex.cn: 1939 年战争爆发前不久他们逃到了美国。

ex.cn: 双方球迷发生了打斗。

ex.cn: 夜间突然发生了火灾。

ex.cn: 从防守高度严密的监狱的集体越狱

ex.cn: 一炮走红的唱片／电影

ex.cn: （全体会议前的）分组会议

ex.cn: 讨论道德问题的小组

ex.cn: 她脸上突然长出一片红疹。

ex.en: He broke out in a cold sweat (= for example, through fear).
ex.cn: 他突然冒出一身冷汗。

senses.def: the point where sth, especially a computer program, is interrupted
senses.chn: （尤指计算机程序的）断点，中断点

senses.def: a point that the person who is serving must win in order not to lose a game
senses.chn: 破发点；破对方发球局的末点

senses.chn: 不支持所属团体（或组织）

senses.def: to stop sb from falling onto sth hard
senses.chn: 缓和某人的跌势；防止某人跌得很重

ex.cn: 幸亏有灌木接着，他摔得不重。

ex.cn: 她取消婚约令他心碎。

ex.en: It breaks my heart to see you like this.
ex.cn: 看到你这个样子我很难过。

to use a lot of physical effort

ex.en: He hardly needed to break sweat to reach the final.
ex.cn: 他几乎不费劲儿就取得了决赛权。

senses.def: to finish the largest or most important part of a task
senses.chn: 完成（任务等的）主要部分

senses.chn: （尤指聚会等开始时，用言语或行动）打破隔阂；打头说话

ex.en: breakthrough technology/products

ex.cn: 示威群众冲破了警方的警戒线。

senses.def: to appear from behind clouds

ex.en: The sun broke through at last in the afternoon.
ex.cn: 下午太阳终于拨云而出。

ex.cn: 他们的婚姻已经破裂。

senses.def: to go away in different directions

ex.cn: 会议在十一点散会。

ex.cn: 你们什么时候放假过圣诞节？

ex.cn: 过度的劳累使他快要垮了。

ex.cn: 伍迪 · 艾伦令我几乎笑破肚皮。

ex.cn: 摒弃传统／旧习惯／过去

either of the two round soft parts at the front of a woman's body that produce milk when she has had a baby

ex.cn: 她开始给婴儿哺乳。

ex.en: breast cancer
ex.cn: 乳腺癌

ex.en: breast milk
ex.cn: 母乳

the top part of the front of your body, below your neck

ex.cn: 他把孩子抱在怀里。

ex.cn: 他的外套胸前别着一排勋章。

senses.def: the front part of a bird's body

ex.cn: 胸部羽毛

ex.cn: 知更鸟的胸部为红色。

senses.def: meat from the front part of the body of a bird or an animal

ex.cn: 鸡／火鸡胸脯肉

ex.en: breast of lamb
ex.cn: 羊羔胸脯肉

senses.def: having the type of chest or breasts mentioned

ex.cn: 乳房小／丰满的女子

ex.en: bare-breasted
ex.cn: 裸胸

ex.en: the yellow-breasted male of the species
ex.cn: 这个物种中有黄色胸部的雄性

senses.def: the part of the body where the feelings and emotions are thought to be

ex.cn: 忧虑的心情

senses.chn: 捶胸顿足（尤指对自己的作为刻意表示悲伤或愧疚）

ex.cn: 他们到达山脊时山谷和湖泊尽收眼底。

ex.cn: 他挺胸顶着波浪大步走进海里。

when a woman breastfeeds, she feeds her baby with milk from her breasts
a piece of armour worn by soldiers in the past to protect the upper front part of the body
a pocket on a shirt, or on the outside or inside of the part of a jacket that covers the chest
a device for getting milk from a woman's breasts, so that her baby can be fed later from a bottle

ex.cn: 他呼出的气中有大蒜味。

ex.en: bad breath (= that smells bad)
ex.cn: 口臭

ex.en: We had to stop for breath before we got to the top.
ex.cn: 我们不得不喘口气，然后再登山顶。

ex.cn: 她呼吸很困难。

senses.def: an amount of air that enters the lungs at one time

ex.en: to take a deep breath
ex.cn: 深深吸一口气

ex.en: He recited the whole poem in one breath.
ex.cn: 他一口气背出了整首诗。

senses.def: a small amount of sth; slight evidence of sth

ex.en: a breath of suspicion/scandal
ex.cn: 一丝怀疑；丑闻的嫌疑

senses.def: a slight movement of air

ex.en: We'll get a breath of fresh air at lunchtime.
ex.cn: 我们午餐时出去透透气。

senses.def: a person, thing or place that is new and different and therefore interesting and exciting
senses.chn: 令人耳目一新的人（或事物、地方）

senses.def: an essential part of a person's existence

to stop breathing for a short time

ex.cn: 屏住呼吸，数到十。

ex.en: He held his breath while the results were read out.
ex.cn: 宣读结果时，他屏住了呼吸。

senses.chn: 别眼巴巴等着；有你等的

ex.cn: 她说她这个星期要干，不过你可别眼巴巴干等！

ex.cn: 他称赞了一番我的工作，但紧接着却对我说不得不辞退我。

senses.chn: （运动后）喘不上气，透不过气来

ex.en: We were out of breath after only five minutes.
ex.cn: 我们五分钟后便气喘吁吁了。

senses.def: to say sth quietly so that people cannot hear

ex.en: 'Rubbish!' he murmured under his breath.
ex.cn: “胡说！” 他悄悄地小声说。

senses.def: to be very surprising or beautiful

ex.en: My first view of the island from the air took my breath away.
ex.cn: 我第一次从空中看到这个岛时，叹赏不已。

senses.def: feeling very anxious or excited

ex.en: We waited with bated breath for the winner to be announced.
ex.cn: 我们屏住呼吸等待宣布冠军是谁。

senses.def: to stop breathing for a moment because of fear, shock, etc.
to breathe normally again after running or doing some tiring exercise
to stop doing sth and rest

ex.en: She talks all the time and hardly stops to draw breath.
ex.cn: 她一直滔滔不绝，几乎没停下来喘口气。

ex.cn: 他是世上少有的大善人。

ex.cn: 不用白费口舌了，你永远说服不了她。

ex.cn: 大多数户外运动服必须透气且防水。

senses.def: to check how much alcohol a driver has drunk by making him or her breathe into a breathalyser
